claims.statement: The built-in Artifact families are atomic-memory, experience, skill, handoff, profile, prompt, and topic-memory; each concrete Artifact type declares its family identifier as a class-level value. The Profile class is bound to PROFILE_FAMILY through its family ClassVar, and ProfileDraft uses the same binding.
The legacy memory family is not a writable or referenceable Artifact family: ArtifactRef rejects family memory, and collection Create and Replace operations for memory are rejected before any write.
Creating an Artifact with the legacy memory family returns 422 with the error code legacy_memory_operation_unsupported and lists Atomic Memory alternatives.
ArtifactRef identifies one exact revision by family, artifact_id, and an integer revision of at least 1, and rejects memory_citations in lineage in favor of Atomic Memory revision citations.

Each Artifact revision is an immutable stored body keyed by scope, family, artifact_id, and revision; the current revision is tracked separately in a head row that advances only by compare-and-set on the previous revision, and a stale advance raises RevisionConflictError.

Revision lineage is stored per revision as direct source evidence, upstream Artifact references, and publication source and digest for copied Artifacts, and it is loaded with each revision rather than being rewritten by later revisions.
The read contract (ArtifactCatalog exposing get, latest, and revisions) is separated from the write contract (ArtifactStore exposing add and revise), so reads do not own writes.
Create (POST /v1/scopes/{scope_id}/artifacts) uses a family-discriminated request union and creates Revision 1; the response sets Location and an ETag of the form revision:1.

Create does not accept a client-chosen Artifact ID: the server generates the ID for most families, Prompt uses its registered prompt_key, and Handoff and Profile use fixed singleton identities; prompt_key is rejected for non-Prompt Creates.

Replace (PUT /v1/scopes/{scope_id}/artifacts/{family}/{artifact_id}) requires an If-Match header: a missing header returns 428 precondition_required, and a value that does not equal the current head's revision ETag returns 412 revision_conflict; the head is checked again inside the write transaction.

Handoff is a Scope singleton: its Create uses the configured Handoff artifact ID (default handoff), returns 409 artifact_already_exists with use_replace set when the singleton already exists, and its Replace must target that configured singleton.

A StableHandle key must match the pattern of lowercase ASCII letters and digits separated by single hyphens and be at most 128 characters; family and key are validated on the handle bind and resolve routes.

Handle bindings are permanent and keyed by (scope_id, family, handle_key): the repository offers only bind and resolve, re-binding the same target returns the existing binding, and binding a different target raises a conflict mapped to HTTP 409 with error code idempotency_conflict.

Binding a handle requires the handle family to match the target family and the target revision to exist in the Scope; a missing target returns not found and resolving an unbound handle returns not found.
Concurrent handle binders resolve through the database unique constraint: the losing transaction re-reads the committed binding and succeeds only when the committed target equals the requested one.

Candidate approval, not direct Create, is the publication path for generated Experience and Skill proposals: approval checks expected_version and then creates a new Artifact under a generated ID when no target exists, or revises the target when one exists.

Profile writes coordinate the Profile policy row and mark the Profile source window dirty before creating or replacing the Profile revision, and restoration by revision requires the restored content to match the historical revision.
Prompt writes validate the content against the registered Prompt operation and publish through the Artifact compare-and-set path, so an invalid Prompt is rejected before any revision is stored.

Atomic Memory Create and Replace are delegated to the Atomic Memory domain writer; Replace compares the caller's ETag with the current revision and passes the expected revision into the prepared command.

Topic Memory content is subject to admission checks that reject recognizable placeholder output and coordination-only text and expect supplied content to be supported by cited evidence or the revised history.
Tags attach to the logical identity (family and artifact_id) rather than to a revision, so they survive content revisions and Server restarts and do not change lineage or embeddings.

Tag labels are normalized to NFC with case folding for matching, reject control, surrogate, and unassigned characters, and are limited to 64 code points per label, 32 labels per target, and 16 labels per filter; normalized duplicates are rejected atomically.
The tag ETag is independent of the revision ETag: tag replacement requires the tag set's ETag in If-Match, and a missing precondition returns 428.
